editorial:
You're back with Star-Lord and his ragtag crew of space misfits. This time, the Guardians are dealing with family drama on a cosmic scale. Peter Quill finally meets his father, Ego, a living planet with big plans. The vibe is colorful, loud, and packed with heart. You'll laugh at Drax's blunt jokes, root for Baby Groot, and feel the tension between Rocket and Yondu. It's a fun ride that leans hard into emotion and never forgets to make you smile.

The action scenes are bright and wild, and the soundtrack is packed with classic hits that fit every moment. The cast brings real warmth, especially Kurt Russell as Ego and Michael Rooker as Yondu. On the downside, the story can feel a bit scattered, and some jokes run a little long. Still, if you love sci-fi adventure with heart, this is for you. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final act, you learn Ego wants to spread himself across the universe and needs Peter's power to do it. Peter refuses and fights his father. Yondu sacrifices himself to save Peter, revealing he was the real father figure all along. The Guardians destroy Ego's core, and Yondu gets a hero's funeral. Peter finally accepts his found family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves sci-fi adventure with heart and humor
